legal.name: Anthropic PBC v. Department of War, et al.
legal.court: U.S. District Court, Northern District of California
legal.status: Summary judgment largely for Anthropic on August 27, 2026; the defendants appealed the preliminary injunction
legal.summary: Anthropic sued after the federal government ordered agencies to stop using its technology and the Department of War labeled it a supply-chain risk. The court ruled the actions were retaliation for protected speech.

evidence.quote: We vigorously challenged the Challenged Actions in Anthropic PBC v. Department of War, et al. (N.D. Cal.) and Anthropic PBC v. Department of War, et al. (D.C. Cir.).
we subsequently, on August 27, 2026, obtained an order from the United States District Court for the Northern District of California that largely granted summary judgment in our favor.

The court ruled that the Challenged Actions were retaliatory acts meant to punish us for speech protected under the First Amendment to the United States Constitution and violated our rights under the Due Process Clause of the Fifth Amendment to the United States Constitution.

legal.name: Anthropic PBC v. Department of War, et al.
legal.court: U.S. Court of Appeals, D.C. Circuit
legal.status: Panel denied the petition 2-1 on September 25, 2026; Anthropic asked for rehearing by the full court
legal.summary: Anthropic challenged the Section 4713 supply-chain risk designation. A divided panel upheld the designation.

evidence.quote: On September 25, 2026, in a 2-1 split decision, the D.C. Circuit Court of Appeals denied our petition for review, ruling that the Department of War’s Section 4713 supply-chain risk designation was proper, and that our rights under the First Amendment and Due Process Clause of the Fifth Amendment were not violated.
We filed a petition for rehearing en banc asking the full D.C. Circuit to review the panel’s decision.
